intelligence.human_view: Harvesting the pricing eye solves the shape; the double layer solves the feel. A flat eye, however correct, is still a picture of an eye — and the Real Object Law says every element is a real physical object, not a flat shape with effects. The double layer is the cheapest honest depth there is: the same thing twice, one behind, shifted just a tad, so the eye has a front and a back and the light has something to catch. It is the same trick he taught for the certificate name — clone behind is the glow/edge layer, the original in front is the solid body — now generalized from a name to any element that needs to feel real. Premium is not a colour or a glow setting; it is depth you can almost touch, and depth comes from layers. The checker does not judge "premium" by taste: the pricing bytes match, and the second layer is visible at 390 and 1440.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine you draw a star on a piece of paper — it's flat, right? Now draw the SAME star on another paper, put it just a tiny bit to the side behind the first one — suddenly your star looks like it's popping right out at you! That's the double layer — two of the same thing, one just a tad behind, and boom, it's real!
intelligence.grandma_view: It's like this, love — one layer is just a picture, dear, but two layers, one tucked just behind the other, and suddenly it has depth, it feels real, like you could reach out and touch it! That's the trick, love — clone it, put it behind, just a tad to the side, and it looks premium, like quality.
intelligence.naya_view: The pricing eye gets more depth — double layer it. Clone it once, put the clone behind, move it right or left just a tad. Premium, quality, maybe glossy — a real element, not a flat picture. The Real Object Law, applied with two layers.
